answer: The signal graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the nectar audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 9 times its size, so a group of 37 keys loses far more than 37 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the tundra checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
